facts.t: The largest local-body award in Finance Commission history
facts.d: ₹7,91,493 crore for rural and urban local bodies together. The urban share rose from roughly 36% under the 15th Commission to 45% — the first time a Commission has tilted so decisively towards cities.

facts.t: Money is now tied to holding elections and publishing accounts
facts.d: Local bodies qualify for grants only if they are duly constituted under Parts IX and IX-A, put their accounts online, and their state has a functioning State Finance Commission with action-taken reports laid before the legislature. Fiscal transfers used as a lever for local democracy.

facts.t: The GDP criterion was deliberately softened
facts.d: Contribution to GDP is moderated by the square root of GSDP, so the largest economies gain without overwhelming the equity component. The unexpected result: the southern states' combined share improved compared with the 15th Commission.

bank.q: The 16th Finance Commission's total award for rural and urban local bodies is approximately:
bank.e: ₹7,91,493 crore in total — ₹4,35,236 crore rural and ₹3,56,257 crore urban.

bank.q: With reference to entry-level conditions for local-body grants, consider the following:
s: Local bodies must be duly constituted under Parts IX and IX-A.
State Finance Commissions must be constituted regularly, with action-taken reports laid before the legislature within six months.
bank.e: All three are required. Together they link money to elections, accounts and transparency — described as the award's strongest institutional reform.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT recommended by the 16th Finance Commission?
o: CAG-certified disclosure of net proceeds under Article 279
A cap on states' fiscal deficit at 3% of GSDP
bank.e: Revenue deficit grants are discontinued, along with sector-specific and state-specific grants — the Commission's single largest departure from its predecessor.

bank.as: The Commission recommended CAG-certified disclosure of net proceeds.
bank.rs: A 41% share of a pool shrunk by cesses and surcharges is not 41% of the Union's total tax effort.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — transparency about the pool's computation is the minimum condition for trust in the devolution figure.

bank.q: Match List I (component) with List II (basis of distribution):
pairs: 2. Gram Panchayat, Block, District where no SFC recommendation exists
3. 90% projected urban population and 10% linked to own-source revenue
bank.e: Urban uses projected urban population with an OSR-linked component; rural uses projected rural population and area; 80:10:10 is the fallback intra-state split; 80:20 is basic to performance.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about the design of local-body grants:
s: Half of basic grants are tied to sanitation, solid waste and water.
Up to 20% of untied funds may be spent on roads.
Untied funds may be used for salaries.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. No portion of the untied grant may be spent on salaries — a deliberate guard against grants becoming establishment funding.

bank.q: The Urbanisation Premium of ₹10,000 crore is a one-time incentive for:
bank.e: Planned rural-to-urban transition. The ₹56,100 crore Special Infrastructure Component covers wastewater management in growth centres of 10 to 40 lakh population.

bank.q: All of the following are criticisms of the 16th Finance Commission's approach EXCEPT:
o: Own-source revenue benchmarks may penalise poor, tribal and hilly Panchayats
Abolishing gap-filling grants may hurt states with structural disadvantages
Climate risks such as heat and flooding receive limited attention
The urban share was reduced relative to the 15th Commission
bank.e: The urban share rose from about 36% to 45% — the highest in Finance Commission history.

bank.q: With reference to own-source revenue targets for Gram Panchayats, consider the following:
s: The target is 1.025 times the previous year or 2.5% compound annual growth, whichever is lower.
A benchmark of ₹1,200 per household per year applies.
bank.e: All three are correct. The Gram Sabha requirement strengthens local democracy, though the benchmarks are criticised as hard for poorer Panchayats to meet.

bank.q: Which article is suggested as the vehicle for targeted equalisation grants addressing structural disadvantage?
bank.e: Article 275 grants-in-aid could serve as an equalisation tool for states with genuine structural disabilities, now that gap-filling grants have been abolished.

bank.as: Dropping the tax-effort criterion may weaken revenue-mobilisation incentives.
bank.rs: GSDP reflects history, geography, ports and agglomeration rather than current policy effort alone.
bank.e: Both are true, but the Reason is a separate criticism of the new GDP criterion rather than an explanation of why dropping tax effort weakens incentives. They are two distinct objections.

bank.q: Arrange the following recommended reforms in the order given as the way forward:
items: Targeted equalisation grants for structural disabilities
Reform cesses through a federal compact
A composite fiscal capacity and service need index
bank.e: Cess reform through a federal compact, then Article 275 equalisation grants, then a composite index, then stronger State Finance Commissions with permanent secretariats.
